Subject: PulseHealth - routing plan for final signatures (MSA + Order Form)

Hi team,

We received PulseHealth's cleanup on the MSA and the Order Form (see attached). Legal has signed off on most redlines but they asked for confirmation of signer authority before we send the envelope. Key asks from the customer:
- One signer on the MSA (CEO) and one on the Order Form (Head of Procurement)
- Witness present for CEO signature (PulseHealth will have a notary at signing)
- They require a final clean PDF and the native audit trail.

Karthik / Priyom — please confirm the DocuSign sequencing you prefer (serial vs parallel), whether we should enable "Sign with ID Check" for the CEO, and if Redwood needs to provide a Power of Attorney template.

Attachments: MSA_PulseHealth_Redlines_v3.docx; OrderForm_PH-0421.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: PulseHealth - routing plan for final signatures (MSA + Order Form)

Marissa — looping in legal (Laura) to confirm the authority items. My preference is serial routing: CEO signs MSA first, then Head of Procurement completes the Order Form. That matches their ask for a witness on the CEO signature and keeps our audit trail simple.

Questions for Laura:
1) Do we need Redwood's POA for the notary (Pulse says their notary will attend on-site)?
2) Any clauses in MSA that should be initialed rather than signed? (I scanned v3 but want legal confirmation.)

I can prepare the envelope drafts once we confirm the signer names and IDs.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PulseHealth - routing plan for final signatures (MSA + Order Form)

Thanks — I reviewed the redlines and have two quick items before we send:

1) Signer authority: please have PulseHealth complete the attached "Signer_Authority_Form_PulseHealth.pdf" and return a corporate resolution or equivalent. We need that on file before countersignature.
2) Notary/Witness: if PulseHealth's notary will be present for the CEO signature, we do not need to provide a POA. However, enable ID verification on the DocuSign envelope for the CEO signatory and include a witness signature field for the notary.

Operational settings for the envelope:
- Routing: Serial (MSA -> Order Form).
- Authentication: ID Check ( government ID photo + SMS OTP) for CEO; SMS OTP for Procurement signer.
- Signing order: 1) Emily Barnes (CEO) 2) Rajiv Kumar (Head of Procurement) — PulseHealth will confirm Rajiv's email, but please instruct they must use the same email that matches the corporate resolution.
- Attachments to include in envelope: final executed MSA PDF, Order Form PDF, Signer Authority Form (signed by customer).

I attached a small markup on v3 (track changes) for two clause tidy-ups (Section 7.3 warranty carve and Section 12.1 audit notice). None of these should block signature.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: Signer_Authority_Form_PulseHealth.pdf

- CEO will present government ID; they prefer we do the ID Check but can accept SMS OTP as secondary.
- Procurement signer (Rajiv) will sign remotely; his email is rajiv.kumar@pulsehealth.com.

Please confirm when Redwood will send the DocuSign envelope (we prefer to have the envelope routed the morning of 5/22 so the notary's attendance is guaranteed).

Attachments: Corp_Resolution_Pulse.pdf; Signer_Authority_Form_PulseHealth.pdf

Emily Barnes
